question: The only Sugar normaly absorbed in the intestine against a concentration gradient is :
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Xylose" -> "passive diffusion" -> "along concentration gradient" -> "no active transport" -> 60%
CHAIN: "Mannose" -> "passive diffusion" -> "along concentration gradient" -> "no active transport" -> 60%
CHAIN: "Ribose" -> "passive diffusion" -> "along concentration gradient" -> "no active transport" -> 60%
analysis: Glucose is the only sugar that is normally absorbed in the intestine against a concentration gradient. This process occurs through active transport mechanisms involving sodium-glucose transport proteins (SGLT1) in the intestinal epithelial cells. The other sugars listed, such as xylose, mannose, and ribose, are absorbed by passive diffusion or facilitated diffusion, which do not occur against a concentration gradient.
